sentences.text: Yandangornis was the second primitive bird genus discovered after Archaeopteryx that possessed a long, bony tail.
This specific characteristic is emphasized in its specific name, longicaudus, which translates to long tail.
It held the distinction of being the second known primitive bird with a long, bony tail after Archaeopteryx.
The genus name honors the Yandang mountains.
The fossil was unearthed in 1986 near Linhai City in Zhejiang Province, China.
Features such as blunt toe claws, a non-reversed hallux, and strong legs suggest a terrestrial mode of life.
Researchers suggest its terrestrial lifestyle may have evolved because its long, heavy tail would have inhibited flying ability.
Cai and Zhao originally classified Yandangornis in the monotypic family Yandangithidae and order Yandangithiformes within the subclass Sauriurae of the class Aves.
Using recent definitions, Yandangornis is not considered a member of the class Aves because it is far more primitive than modern birds.
Zhou and Zhang (2007) noted that Yandangornis's affinities were poorly diagnosed and suggested it might be a non-avialan theropod.
Zhou and Zhang (2007) pointed out that Yandangornis's affinities were not sufficiently studied and that it could be a non-avian theropod genus.
Yandangornis is poorly documented in the literature and has been omitted from recent reevaluations of avialan systematics.
The time range for Yandangornis is recorded as Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago).
